name: Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC)
measures: Curated datasets, splits and leaderboards across ADMET, drug-target interaction, generation and clinical tasks.
caveat: Many ADMET sets are small; leaderboard gaps are often within seed-to-seed variance.

name: MoleculeNet
measures: Classic property benchmarks (BBBP, ESOL, Lipophilicity, ClinTox, BACE, HIV, Tox21 and more).
caveat: Widely criticised for invalid or duplicate structures, inconsistent labels and splits that vary between papers.

name: Open Graph Benchmark: molecules
measures: ogbg-molhiv and ogbg-molpcba with fixed scaffold splits, evaluators and a public leaderboard.
caveat: molhiv has few positives, so ranks swing with random seeds; leaderboard entries are self-reported.

name: Polaris
measures: Hub of community-certified datasets and benchmarks with standard evaluation.
caveat: Young ecosystem; dataset quality and certification depth vary by contributor.

name: MoleculeACE
measures: Prediction on activity cliffs: near-identical molecules with very different potency across ChEMBL targets.
caveat: Cliff definitions depend on similarity and potency thresholds; covers a fixed set of targets.

name: PoseBusters
measures: Physical and chemical plausibility checks for predicted protein-ligand poses, plus a held-out benchmark set.
caveat: Plausible is not correct: passing checks says nothing about affinity, and the test set is modest in size.

name: PDBbind / CASF
measures: Experimental binding affinities for PDB complexes; CASF core sets for scoring, ranking, docking and screening power.
caveat: Protein and ligand similarity between the general set and core set leaks information into many reported results.

name: DUD-E
measures: Actives and property-matched decoys for virtual-screening enrichment across ~100 targets.
caveat: Decoy construction bias lets ML models separate actives from decoys without learning binding.

name: LIT-PCBA
measures: Virtual-screening sets built from PubChem confirmatory assays with true inactives.
caveat: Very low active counts on several targets make enrichment metrics noisy.

name: GuacaMol
caveat: Many goal-directed tasks are saturated and can be gamed with unrealistic molecules.

name: MOSES
measures: Distribution-learning metrics for generative models on a ZINC-derived set.
caveat: Validity, uniqueness and novelty are near-saturated and say little about usefulness.

name: USPTO-50k
measures: Single-step retrosynthesis on ~50k patent reactions with reaction-class labels.
caveat: Top-k exact match penalises valid alternative routes; atom-mapping artefacts remain.

name: PrimeKG
measures: Precision-medicine knowledge graph of diseases, drugs, genes, phenotypes and pathways, used for target and repurposing tasks.
caveat: A snapshot of its sources; link-prediction splits leak if reverse and duplicate edges aren't removed.

name: Hetionet
measures: Integrative network of 11 node types used for drug-repurposing prediction.
caveat: Built in 2017 and not updated; newer drugs and associations are missing.

name: Insilico DDD Benchmarks (BaaS)
measures: Commercial benchmark service: Drug Discovery Foundations task suite and end-to-end Drug Candidate Essentials.
caveat: Items and scoring are proprietary and run server-side, so results can't be independently reproduced.

name: O3DC Benchmark Index
measures: Community index of drug-discovery benchmarks with maintainers, repo activity and known caveats.
caveat: Convened by Insilico, which also lists its own commercial products in the index.
